translationRepairs: Dividing the dividend by the divisor yields winter solstice's added hour at thirty-one ke after midnight—one day later than the Yuankai Calendar, which matches the true count of celestial days.
Dividing the dividend by the divisor yields winter solstice's added hour at thirty-one ke after midnight—one day later than the Yuanjia Calendar, which matches the true count of celestial days.
Source 《元嘉曆》 is the Yuanjia Calendar (元嘉); Yuankai misreads 嘉 as kai, and the proposed Yuanjia restores the correct calendar name without other changes.
Divide the dividend by the divisor; one obtains winter solstice's added hour at thirty-one ke after midnight, one day later than the Yuankai Calendar—the correct reckoning of heaven's days.
Divide the dividend by the divisor; one obtains winter solstice's added hour at thirty-one ke after midnight, one day later than the Yuanjia Calendar—the correct reckoning of heaven's days.
The same 《元嘉曆》 must be Yuanjia in the literal field; Yuankai is a pinyin error, and the replacement corrects only that name.
In the third year of the Xiaping era of Later Han, the Monograph on the Quarter-remainder Calendar records the mid-term shadow at Start of Winter as 1 zhang and at Beginning of Spring as 9 chi 6 cun.
In the third year of the Xiping era of Later Han, the Monograph on the Quarter-remainder Calendar records the mid-term shadow at Start of Winter as 1 zhang and at Beginning of Spring as 9 chi 6 cun.
Source 熹平三年 uses the era 熹平, standard pinyin Xiping; Xiaping invents an incorrect first syllable, and the proposed form matches the Chinese era name.
In Xiaping year 3, the calendar then in use fixed the winter solstice on dingchou, with the added hour exactly at midday.
In Xiping year 3, the calendar then in use fixed the winter solstice on dingchou, with the added hour exactly at midday.
Unit 熹平三年 again names the Xiping era; idiomatic Xiaping is the same misspelling, and Xiping is the accurate repair.
